mainTopic: Women's obligations in time-bound מצוות‎, קידוש and ברכת המזון, and whether הרהור counts as דיבור for a בעל קרי
overview: This amud finishes the משנה: women, slaves and minors are exempt from קריאת שמע and תפילין, but they are obligated in תפילה, מזוזה and ברכת המזון. For each item, the גמרא asks why the משנה needed to say it. Each time it answers with מהו דתימא / קמשמע לן, showing a mistake one might have made. רב אדא בר אהבה then rules that women are obligated in קידוש from the תורה, even though it is time-bound. אביי says the obligation is only rabbinic, but רבא rejects this and derives a Torah obligation from the link between זכור and שמור. רבינא asks whether women's ברכת המזון obligation is דאורייתא or דרבנן, and a proof from a ברייתא is turned aside. An אגדה then praises Israel for saying ברכת המזון even on a כזית or כביצה. A new משנה follows about a בעל קרי, and the גמרא brings two opposite readings of it: רבינא says הרהור counts like דיבור, and רב חסדא says it does not.

steps.title: The משנה's list of exemptions and obligations
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its ruling. Women, slaves and minors are exempt from תפילין. They are obligated in תפילה, מזוזה and ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and they are exempt from תפילין. But they are obligated in תפילה, in מזוזה, and in ברכת המזון.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the משנה, which started on the previous daf. It lists the מצוות that women, slaves and minors are exempt from, and the ones they must still do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has two lists. The first is an exemption list: קריאת שמע and תפילין. The second is an obligation list: תפילה, מזוזה and ברכת המזון. The גמרא is about to go through each item and ask why the משנה had to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: Phylacteries worn on the arm and head

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up תְּפִילִּין (tefillin, which women are exempt from) with תְּפִילָּה (prayer, which women are obligated in). The two words look almost the same, but the משנה gives them opposite rulings.

phrases.english: and from tefillin,
phrases.notes: Continues the exemption list from the previous daf: women, slaves and minors are exempt from קריאת שמע and from תפילין.

phrases.english: but they are obligated in prayer
and in mezuza and in Grace after Meals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה begun on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women, slaves and minors are exempt from קריאת שמע and תפילין. They are obligated in תפילה, מזוזה and ברכת המזון.

steps.title: Why say women are exempt from קריאת שמע? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needed to say that women are exempt from קריאת שמע. It is a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, and women are exempt from all such מצוות anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא. About קריאת שמע: Isn't that obvious? It is a positive מצוה that depends on time, and women are exempt from every positive מצוה that depends on time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion with an 'obviousness' challenge. Why did the משנה write something we already know from a general rule?
steps.deeperAnalysis: קריאת שמע is said only at certain times, morning and night. That makes it a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא. A known rule already exempts women from all such מצוות, so listing קריאת שמע seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
A positive מצוה caused (limited) by time

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that women are exempt from a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא is a foundational principle across all of ש"ס. Here it is treated as so well known that restating it seems pointless.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Regarding Shema: it is obvious!
It is a positive מצוה caused by time,
phrases.notes: קריאת שמע is recited only in the morning and at night.

phrases.english: and from every positive מצוה caused by time
women are exempt?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the first item in the משנה's exemption list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's explicit mention that women are exempt from קריאת שמע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general rule exempting women from a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא already covers קריאת שמע, so the משנה's statement seems redundant.

steps.title: שמע contains accepting God's kingship, yet women are still exempt
steps.stepSummary: One might have thought קריאת שמע is special because it contains קבלת מלכות שמים, and so women would be obligated. The משנה teaches that they are exempt anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since קריאת שמע contains מלכות שמים, women should be obligated. So the משנה teaches us that they are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains what mistake the משנה is protecting us from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קריאת שמע is not just any time-bound מצוה. It is the acceptance of God's kingship, which might seem important enough to apply to everyone. The משנה makes clear that the general exemption still applies, despite this special content.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (this is the mistake we could have made)
The kingship of Heaven (accepting God as King)

phrases.english: Lest you say:
since it contains the kingship of Heaven,
phrases.notes: So one might think women would be obligated despite the time limit.

phrases.english: it teaches us (that they are exempt).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְתֵימָא: הוֹאִיל וְאִית בַּהּ מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge about קריאת שמע.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: the statement is needed to block a reasonable mistaken assumption.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because קריאת שמע contains מלכות שמים, women might be obligated despite it being time-bound.
steps.terutzMaskana: The general exemption for a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא applies. Women are exempt from קריאת שמע.

steps.title: Why say women are exempt from תפילין? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about תפילין. They are also time-bound, so the women's exemption seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from תפילין: Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה and asks the same 'why say it?' question. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תפילין are worn by day and not at night, on weekdays and not on שבת or יום טוב. That makes them a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא too, so the general rule should already exempt women.

phrases.english: And from tefillin.
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the משנה.

phrases.english: It is obvious!
phrases.notes: תפילין are not worn at night or on שבת and יום טוב, so they are time-bound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the same type of challenge, now aimed at the second item in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's explicit mention that women are exempt from תפילין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תפילין are a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, so the general rule already exempts women.

steps.title: תפילין is linked to מזוזה, yet women are still exempt
steps.stepSummary: One might have thought that because the תורה places תפילין next to מזוזה, women would be obligated in תפילין just as they are in מזוזה. The משנה teaches that they are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since תפילין is compared to מזוזה (which women must do), women should be obligated in תפילין too. So the משנה teaches us that they are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה needed to block a mistake. Someone could think תפילין follows the rule of מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פרשה of שמע, the verse about תפילין is followed directly by the verse about מזוזה. This creates a היקש, a comparison between them. Women are obligated in מזוזה, which is not time-bound, so one might think the היקש obligates them in תפילין too. The משנה teaches that the time-bound rule wins and women are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: It is compared (linked by a היקש, a juxtaposition in the verses)
A comparison drawn from two topics placed side by side in the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: The היקש does not make תפילין into something other than a time-bound מצוה. The point is only that one might have expected the link to מזוזה to override the exemption. The משנה says it does not.
steps.whatToRemember: Both קריאת שמע and תפילין are a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, so women are exempt. The משנה still mentions each one, because each has a feature that might have suggested an exception: מלכות שמים for קריאת שמע, and the היקש to מזוזה for תפילין.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
since it is juxtaposed to mezuza —
phrases.notes: דברים ו:ח (תפילין) is followed by ו:ט (מזוזה). Women are obligated in מזוזה.

phrases.english: it teaches us (that they are exempt).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge about תפילין.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: the statement is needed to block a mistake based on a היקש.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because תפילין is compared to מזוזה, women might be obligated in תפילין just as they are in מזוזה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The time-bound exemption applies. Women are exempt from תפילין despite the היקש.

steps.title: Women are obligated in prayer because prayer is a request for mercy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that women are obligated in תפילה and gives the reason: תפילה is asking for mercy, and everyone needs mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they are obligated in prayer.' Because prayer is a request for mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the משנה, women's obligation in תפילה, and gives a short reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Prayer happens at set times, so you might expect women to be exempt like other time-bound מצוות. The גמרא explains that תפילה is basically asking ה׳ for mercy, and women need mercy just like men. So they are obligated.

phrases.english: And they are obligated in prayer.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: Because it is a request for mercy.
phrases.notes: The reason women are included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the exemptions (קריאת שמע, תפילין) to the obligations listed in the משנה, starting with תפילה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Women are obligated in תפילה because prayer is a plea for mercy, which everyone needs.

steps.title: Why the משנה needed to say women must pray
steps.stepSummary: Even though the reason is simple, the משנה had to say it. Otherwise one might think that because a פסוק mentions evening, morning and afternoon, prayer counts as a time-bound מצוה, which would exempt women.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since it is written about prayer 'Evening, morning and afternoon', it is like a time-bound positive מצוה. So the משנה teaches us that women are still obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה bothered to say that women must pray. It shows the mistake someone could have made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'עֶרֶב וָבֹקֶר וְצָהֳרַיִם' ties prayer to fixed times of day. That could make it look like a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, which would exempt women. The משנה tells us not to think that way: prayer's main nature is mercy, so women are obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a possible mistake)
So it teaches us (the משנה rules out the mistake)
A positive מצוה that depends on a set time. Women are generally exempt from these.

steps.confusionAlert: There is no explicit question here, but this line still answers one. The 'מהו דתימא… קמשמע לן' formula always explains why the משנה needed to say something that seemed obvious.

phrases.english: You might have said: since it is written about it,
'Evening and morning and afternoon',
phrases.notes: תהלים נה:יח

phrases.english: it is like a time-bound positive מצוה,
so it teaches us (that they are obligated).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the משנה had to state the ruling from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Justifying the משנה's wording by showing a possible mistake (הוה אמינא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because a פסוק links prayer to set times, it would be a time-bound מצוה and women would be exempt.

steps.title: מזוזה: isn't it obvious women are obligated?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that women are obligated in מזוזה and asks why this needed to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And in מזוזה.' That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next obligation in the משנה, מזוזה, and challenges it as too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מזוזה is a positive מצוה that has nothing to do with time. Women are only exempt from time-bound מצוות, so of course they are obligated in מזוזה. Why would the משנה spell it out?

keyTerms.meaning: The scroll fixed on the doorpost
It is obvious! (a challenge that something did not need to be said)

phrases.english: And in mezuzah. That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as before, now applied to מזוזה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that women are obligated in מזוזה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מזוזה is not time-bound, so women's obligation is obvious and did not need to be stated.

steps.title: מזוזה is linked to תלמוד תורה, which women are exempt from
steps.stepSummary: One might have thought women are exempt from מזוזה because the תורה places it right next to תלמוד תורה, and women are exempt from תלמוד תורה. The משנה teaches that they are still obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since מזוזה is compared to תלמוד תורה (and women are exempt from תלמוד תורה, they should be exempt from מזוזה). So the משנה teaches us that they are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing a mistake someone could have made about מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פרשה of שמע (דברים יא:יט–כ), the פסוק about teaching Torah comes right before the פסוק about מזוזה. This kind of link (a היקש) could suggest the two have the same rules, so women would be exempt from מזוזה as they are from תלמוד תורה. The משנה rejects that.

keyTerms.meaning: It was compared or linked (by a היקש, placing two topics side by side in the תורה)

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the reverse of step 5. There, being linked to מזוזה might have made women obligated in תפילין. Here, being linked to תלמוד תורה might have made women exempt from מזוזה. Both times, the משנה blocks the comparison.

phrases.english: You might have said: since
it is compared to Torah study,
phrases.notes: דברים יא:יט–כ

phrases.english: so it teaches us (that they are obligated).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְתֵימָא: הוֹאִיל וְאִתַּקַּשׁ לְתַלְמוּד תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Justifying the משנה's wording by showing a possible mistake (הוה אמינא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because מזוזה is linked to תלמוד תורה, women would be exempt from it.

steps.title: ברכת המזון: isn't it obvious women are obligated?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that women are obligated in ברכת המזון and challenges it as obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And in ברכת המזון.' That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the last obligation in the משנה, ברכת המזון, and again asks why it needed to be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You say ברכת המזון whenever you eat, at any time. So it is not time-bound, and women should obviously be obligated. The challenge is why the משנה stated it.

phrases.english: And in Grace after Meals. That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same פשיטא pattern, now applied to ברכת המזון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that women are obligated in ברכת המזון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ברכת המזון is not time-bound, so women's obligation is obvious.

steps.title: A verse links meals to evening and morning
steps.stepSummary: One might have thought ברכת המזון is time-bound because a פסוק speaks of meat in the evening and bread in the morning. The משנה teaches that women are still obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since it is written 'When ה׳ gives you meat to eat in the evening and bread in the morning to be satisfied', it is like a time-bound positive מצוה. So the משנה teaches us that women are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing a mistake someone could have made about ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in שמות טז:ח describes meals at set times (evening and morning). That might suggest meals, and so the ברכה after them, are tied to time, which would exempt women. The משנה makes clear that ברכת המזון is not time-bound and women are obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: When ה׳ gives you (שמות טז:ח, about the מן and the quail)
To be satisfied, to the full

steps.whatToRemember: All three obligations follow the same pattern. Each seemed obvious, but each had a 'hook' (a פסוק about times, or a היקש) that could have misled us. The משנה spelled them out to block those mistakes.

phrases.english: You might have said: since it is written,
'When the Lord gives you meat to eat in the evening'
phrases.notes: שמות טז:ח

phrases.english: 'and bread in the morning to the full',
it is like a time-bound positive מצוה,
so it teaches us (that they are obligated).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְתֵימָא הוֹאִיל וּכְתִיב ״בְּתֵת ה׳ לָכֶם בָּעֶרֶב בָּשָׂר לֶאֱכֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Justifying the משנה's wording by showing a possible mistake (הוה אמינא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because a פסוק links meals to evening and morning, ברכת המזון would be time-bound and women would be exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Women are obligated in ברכת המזון.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: women are obligated in קידוש from the תורה
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה rules that women are obligated in קידוש היום on שבת by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: Women are obligated in sanctifying the day (קידוש) by Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the משנה's list is finished, the גמרא brings a new statement from an אמורא about another מצוה for women: קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is new information beyond the משנה. רב אדא בר אהבה says women's obligation in קידוש is דאורייתא, from the תורה itself. This sets up a problem, because קידוש happens only on שבת, a set time.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who makes this ruling

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
Women are obligated in the sanctification of the day
by Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: נָשִׁים חַיָּיבוֹת בְּקִדּוּשׁ הַיּוֹם דְּבַר תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. After finishing the משנה's list, the גמרא brings an אמורא's ruling about another מצוה for women.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women are obligated in קידוש היום מדאורייתא.

steps.title: But קידוש is a time-bound מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אדא בר אהבה: קידוש depends on a set time (שבת), and women are exempt from all time-bound positive מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? It is a time-bound positive מצוה, and women are exempt from every time-bound positive מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling using the general rule that women are exempt from time-bound מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידוש is said only on שבת, so it is clearly time-bound. The general rule exempts women from all such מצוות. So how can רב אדא say women are obligated from the תורה?

keyTerms.meaning: All, every (the rule covers every case)

phrases.english: Why?
It is a time-bound positive מצוה,
and from every time-bound positive מצוה
women are exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's claim that women are obligated in קידוש from the תורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קידוש is time-bound, and the general rule exempts women from all time-bound positive מצוות.

steps.title: אביי: the obligation is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that women are obligated in קידוש only מדרבנן (rabbinically), not from the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is a rabbinic obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by reducing the level of women's obligation in קידוש from Torah law to rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי accepts the challenge: by Torah law, women would be exempt from קידוש because it is time-bound. He explains that their obligation comes from the רבנן. This reads רב אדא's 'Torah law' as not meant literally.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law (the opposite of מדרבנן)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final word. In the next step, רבא challenges אביי, since רב אדא clearly said 'Torah law'. Step 16 then gives a different answer that keeps the obligation דאורייתא.

phrases.english: Abaye said: By rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by lowering the obligation to the rabbinic level.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the level of obligation (rabbinic rather than Torah)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Women's obligation in קידוש is from the תורה, which conflicts with the time-bound rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to אביי, women's obligation in קידוש is only מדרבנן, so the general rule stays intact.

steps.title: רבא rejects אביי's answer with two objections
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives two objections to אביי. First, רב אדא בר אהבה explicitly said 'by Torah law.' Second, if חז״ל could obligate women in קידוש, they should obligate them in every positive time-bound מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But רב אדא said 'by Torah law'! And furthermore, if so, let us obligate women in every positive מצוה rabbinically!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on אביי's answer from Step 14 and says it cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His first objection is about wording: רב אדא בר אהבה clearly said 'דבר תורה,' so a rabbinic reading contradicts his own words. His second objection is about logic: nothing makes קידוש special. If חז״ל could obligate women here, why not in every מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא?

phrases.english: Rava said to him (to Abaye):
But he (Rav Adda) said 'by Torah law'!
phrases.notes: Objection 1: אביי's reading contradicts the wording.

phrases.english: And furthermore, every positive מצוה:
let us obligate them (women) in it rabbinically!
phrases.notes: Objection 2: אביי's logic would apply everywhere.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וְהָא ״דְּבַר תּוֹרָה״ קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's answer from Step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects אביי's claim that women's קידוש is only rabbinic.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It contradicts רב אדא's explicit 'דבר תורה,' and it gives no reason why קידוש would be singled out over every other time-bound מצוה.

steps.title: רבא's answer: whoever must observe שבת must also remember it
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains why women are obligated in קידוש מדאורייתא. The Torah pairs זכור with שמור, so anyone obligated in שמירת שבת is also obligated in זכירה. Women are obligated in שמירה, so they are obligated in זכירה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The verse says 'זכור' and 'שמור.' Whoever is included in observing is included in remembering. Since women are included in observing, they are included in remembering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer to the question from Step 13, defending רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One version of the עשרת הדברות says 'זכור' and the other says 'שמור,' so the two are linked as one package. Women must keep the לאוין of שבת, which are שמירה, just like men. Because of the link, they are also included in the positive מצוה of זכירה (קידוש), even though it is time-bound.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Remember' (the positive מצוה of Shabbat, fulfilled through קידוש)

steps.whatToRemember: Women are obligated in קידוש מדאורייתא because of the היקש of זכור and שמור. Whoever is bound by שמירה is bound by זכירה.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel the general rule that women are exempt from time-bound positive מצוות. It is a specific exception created by the link between זכור and שמור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for women's Torah-level obligation in קידוש. It later matters for whether a woman can be מוציא a man in קידוש.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
The verse says 'Remember' and 'Observe':
phrases.notes: Exodus 20:8 and Deuteronomy 5:12.

phrases.english: whoever is included in observing
is included in remembering.
And these women, since they are included in observing,
they are included in remembering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: אָמַר קְרָא ״זָכוֹר וְשָׁמוֹר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting אביי's answer, רבא offers his own answer to the קשיא of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural derivation that creates an exception to a general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קידוש is time-bound, so women should be exempt, or at most obligated rabbinically.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because זכור is linked to שמור, women are obligated in קידוש מדאורייתא.

steps.title: רבינא asks: are women obligated in ברכת המזון by Torah or rabbinic law?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רבא whether women's obligation in ברכת המזון is Torah-level or rabbinic. The practical difference is whether a woman can be מוציא others. Someone with only a rabbinic obligation counts as 'not obligated' and cannot exempt people who have a Torah obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא asked רבא: Are women obligated in ברכת המזון by Torah law or rabbinic law? What difference does it make? Whether they can fulfill the obligation of others. If it is Torah law, one with a Torah obligation can exempt others with a Torah obligation. If it is rabbinic, she counts as 'not obligated,' and someone not obligated cannot exempt others. So what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא opens a new question about the משנה's ruling on women and ברכת המזון, and explains why the answer matters in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 established that women are obligated, but not at what level. To be מוציא someone, the person reciting must have the same level of obligation as the listener. A woman with only a rabbinic obligation could not exempt a man who is obligated מדאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?
To fulfill others' obligation on their behalf
One who is not obligated in the matter

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the general principle that only someone who shares the obligation at the same level can be מוציא others.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rava:
Women in Grace after Meals:
is it by Torah law or by rabbinic law?
What difference does it make?
To fulfill the obligation of the many.
Granted, if you say it is Torah law,
one with a Torah obligation comes and exempts those with a Torah obligation.
But if you say it is rabbinic,
she is 'one who is not obligated in the matter,'
and anyone not obligated in the matter

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ מוֹצִיא אֶת הָרַבִּים יְדֵי חוֹבָתָן.
phrases.english: cannot fulfill the obligation of the many.
So what is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרָבָא: נָשִׁים בְּבִרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן, דְאוֹרָיְיתָא אוֹ דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from קידוש back to the משנה's ruling on ברכת המזון, asking the same Torah-or-rabbinic question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether women's obligation in ברכת המזון is Torah-level or rabbinic, which decides whether a woman can be מוציא others.

steps.title: An attempted proof from a ברייתא: a wife may bless for her husband
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a son may bless for his father, a slave for his master, and a wife for her husband, though חכמים cursed a man who needs this. Since a wife can be מוציא her husband, this seems to show that her obligation is מדאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: They truly said that a son may bless on behalf of his father, a slave on behalf of his master, and a woman on behalf of her husband. But חכמים said: May a curse come upon a man whose wife and children bless for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רבינא's question with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a woman can recite ברכת המזון on her husband's behalf. If women were only rabbinically obligated, she could not exempt his Torah obligation. So the ברייתא seems to prove that women are obligated מדאורייתא. The curse is not about the halacha; it criticizes a man too ignorant to bless for himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a proof from a source)
'In truth they said,' which introduces an established halacha

steps.confusionAlert: The curse does not mean the wife's blessing is invalid. It works halachically; the curse is aimed at the husband's ignorance.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
In truth they said:
a son may bless on behalf of his father,
and a slave may bless on behalf of his master,
and a woman may bless on behalf of her husband,
but the Sages said:
May a curse come upon a man
whose wife and children bless on his behalf.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: בֶּאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ בֵּן מְבָרֵךְ לְאָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to resolve רבינא's question from Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That women's obligation in ברכת המזון is מדאורייתא, since a wife can be מוציא her husband.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that a son, slave, and wife may bless on behalf of father, master, and husband.

steps.title: Finishing the proof: only a Torah obligation can exempt a Torah obligation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the logic of the ברייתא proof. A wife can be מוציא her husband only if her obligation is דאורייתא, like his.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if you say her obligation is from the Torah: someone obligated by the Torah can come and exempt someone obligated by the Torah. But if you say her obligation is only rabbinic, can someone with a rabbinic obligation come and exempt someone with a Torah obligation?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof it started in the last step. It explains why the ברייתא shows that a woman's ברכת המזון obligation is from the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that you can only exempt someone whose obligation is the same level as yours or lower. A husband who ate and was satisfied has a Torah obligation. So if his wife can exempt him, her obligation must also be Torah-level.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (the first option works fine)
Comes and exempts (fulfills the obligation for someone else)

phrases.english: Granted, if you say it is by Torah law,
one obligated by Torah law comes and exempts one obligated by Torah law.
But if you say it is rabbinic,
can one obligated rabbinically come and exempt one obligated by Torah law?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question. The answer is obviously no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That a woman's obligation in ברכת המזון is דאורייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא saying a wife may bless for her husband, combined with the rule that a rabbinic obligation cannot exempt a Torah obligation.

steps.title: But a minor is also listed, and he has no Torah obligation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the proof. The same ברייתא says a son may bless for his father, and a קטן is not obligated in מצוות at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, is a minor obligated in מצוות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It points out that the ברייתא also lets a young son bless for his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא means the father has a Torah obligation, then the קטן could never exempt him, since a קטן has no Torah obligation. So the ברייתא cannot be talking about a Torah-level case. That means the wife's case proves nothing either.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning (turning your logic back on you)
A minor (a child below the age of מצוות)

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, is a minor someone who is obligated?
phrases.notes: Everyone agrees a קטן is exempt by Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in steps 18–19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא. It does not rule on the original question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the ברייתא is about a Torah-level obligation. But the קטן in the same list shows it cannot be.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about someone who ate only a rabbinic-sized amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reinterprets the ברייתא. It is talking about a father who ate only a small amount, which requires ברכת המזון only מדרבנן. So rabbinic obligations exempt rabbinic obligations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what case are we dealing with here? Where he ate only the rabbinic measure, so someone with a rabbinic obligation comes and exempts someone with a rabbinic obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new way to read the ברייתא, so that the קטן case makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה requires ברכת המזון only when you are full (ושבעת). The רבנן added an obligation for a small amount, like a כזית or כביצה. In that case the father's obligation is only rabbinic. So a son, a slave, or a wife, even if their own obligation is rabbinic, can exempt him.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrower reading of a source)

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the ברייתא falls away, and the גמרא here does not decide רבינא's question. It stays open whether a woman's ברכת המזון obligation is דאורייתא or דרבנן.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer does NOT prove that a woman's obligation is rabbinic. It only shows that the ברייתא cannot be used as proof either way.

phrases.english: Rather, with what are we dealing here?
For example, where he ate a rabbinic measure,
phrases.notes: An amount that does not make him full, such as a כזית or כביצה.

phrases.english: so one obligated rabbinically comes and exempts one obligated rabbinically.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the alternative reading of the ברייתא that step 20's objection requires.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is about a rabbinic-level meal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about a full, Torah-level meal, so the wife must be obligated מדאורייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a rabbinic-sized meal, so it says nothing about the level of a woman's obligation.

steps.title: The angels ask: why does הקב״ה show favor to Israel?
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא teaches an אגדה. The ministering angels point out a contradiction: the תורה says הקב״ה does not show favor, yet ברכת כהנים says He does show favor to Israel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוירא taught, sometimes in the name of רבי אמי and sometimes in the name of רבי אסי: The מלאכי השרת said before הקב״ה: 'Master of the world, it is written in Your תורה, "Who does not show favor and does not take a bribe." Yet You show favor to Israel, as it is written, "May ה׳ lift up His face to you"!'
steps.whatsHappening: The rabbinic measure for ברכת המזון was just mentioned, so the גמרא brings a related אגדה. This step sets up the angels' question; הקב״ה's answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angels contrast two פסוקים. One says הקב״ה is a judge who never plays favorites. The other, from ברכת כהנים, asks Him to lift His face toward Israel and treat them with special favor.

phrases.english: Rav Avira taught,

phrases.aramaic: זִמְנִין אָמַר לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי
phrases.english: sometimes he said it in the name of Rabbi Ami

phrases.aramaic: וְזִמְנִין אָמַר לַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: and sometimes he said it in the name of Rabbi Asi:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: The ministering angels said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world, it is written in Your Torah:

phrases.aramaic: ״אֲשֶׁר לֹא יִשָּׂא פָנִים וְלֹא יִקַּח שֹׁחַד״,
phrases.english: "Who does not show favor and does not take a bribe" (Devarim 10:17),
yet You show favor to Israel,
as it is written: "May ה׳ lift up His face to you" (Bamidbar 6:26)?!
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from ברכת כהנים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An associative move: step 21 mentioned the rabbinic measure for ברכת המזון, and this אגדה is about that same measure.
steps.kashyaTarget: The apparent contradiction between Devarim 10:17 and Bamidbar 6:26.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A God who shows no favoritism should not single out Israel for special favor.

steps.title: Israel goes beyond the law, so they deserve favor
steps.stepSummary: הקב״ה answers that the תורה only requires ברכת המזון when one is full. Israel is strict with itself and says ברכת המזון even on a כזית or כביצה, so they deserve special favor.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'How can I not show favor to Israel? I wrote for them in the תורה, "You shall eat, and be satisfied, and bless ה׳ your God," and they are strict with themselves even for a כזית or a כביצה!'
steps.whatsHappening: הקב״ה answers the angels' question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה obligation begins only with being full (ושבעת). Israel takes on the obligation even for a small amount. Because they go beyond what is required of them, הקב״ה goes beyond strict judgment for them. This is measure for measure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This אגדה shows that saying ברכת המזון on a small amount is a rabbinic extension of the Torah law. That is the same point the halachic answer in step 21 relied on.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: וְכִי לֹא אֶשָּׂא פָּנִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: He said to them: And how can I not show favor to Israel,
for I wrote for them in the Torah:
"And you shall eat and be satisfied, and bless ה׳ your God" (Devarim 8:10),
and they are strict with themselves
even down to an olive-size and an egg-size.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם וְכִי לֹא אֶשָּׂא פָּנִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the angels' question from step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Israel goes beyond the Torah's requirement in ברכת המזון, so הקב״ה goes beyond strict justice in showing them favor.

steps.title: New משנה: what a בעל קרי may and may not say
steps.stepSummary: A בעל קרי thinks שמע in his heart and does not say its ברכות before or after. For food, he says the after-blessing but not the before-blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A בעל קרי thinks the words in his heart, and does not say the blessings, neither before it nor after it. And over food he says the blessing afterward, but he does not say the blessing beforehand.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It discusses what someone who is טמא from a seminal emission may say, based on עזרא's decree that such a person may not engage in Torah matters until he immerses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For קריאת שמע, he only thinks the words and skips the ברכות entirely. For food, he says the after-blessing because ברכת המזון is a Torah obligation. He skips the before-blessing, which is only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
Someone טמא from a seminal emission
Thinks it in his heart (without saying it aloud)
Before it and after it (the ברכות surrounding שמע)

steps.confusionAlert: 'לפניה ולאחריה' refers to the ברכות of קריאת שמע. 'לפניו ולאחריו' refers to the blessings over food. These are two separate cases with different rules.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who is tamei from a seminal emission —
thinks it in his heart, and does not recite the blessings,
phrases.notes: He thinks the words of שמע without saying them aloud.

phrases.english: neither before it nor after it.
And over food, he recites the blessing afterward,
phrases.notes: ברכת המזון is a Torah obligation.

phrases.english: but does not recite the blessing beforehand.
phrases.notes: The blessing before eating is rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It still connects to the theme of Torah-level versus rabbinic blessings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בעל קרי thinks שמע in his heart without its ברכות. For food, he says only the after-blessing.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: he says the blessings before and after
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees. A בעל קרי may say the blessings both before and after, for שמע and for food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He recites the blessings before them and after them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a dissenting opinion to the first view in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Them' (לפניהם ולאחריהם) is plural, covering both שמע and food. רבי יהודה does not limit the בעל קרי the way the תנא קמא does; he allows all the ברכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Before them and after them (both cases)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two views. The תנא קמא limits a בעל קרי to Torah-level blessings only, and only thinking for שמע. רבי יהודה allows all the blessings.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He recites the blessings before them and after them.
phrases.notes: Covers both שמע and food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissent from the ruling of the תנא קמא in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בעל קרי recites the blessings before and after, both for שמע and for food.

steps.title: רבינא: Thinking the words counts like saying them
steps.stepSummary: רבינא learns from the משנה that הרהור is like דיבור. Otherwise there would be no point in the בעל קרי thinking שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבינא said: This teaches that thinking is like speaking. Because if you thought it is not like speaking, why would he think the words at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא section on our משנה begins. רבינא draws a lesson from the rule that a בעל קרי thinks שמע in his heart: thinking counts like saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה tells the בעל קרי to think שמע silently. רבינא reasons that this instruction only makes sense if thinking actually accomplishes something, such as fulfilling the מצוה. If thinking did nothing, the משנה would have no reason to ask for it.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches / this shows (a lesson learned from a source)
Thinking the words in one's mind
Speech, saying the words out loud
For if you would think (sets up an 'otherwise' argument)

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not saying a בעל קרי may speak out loud. He agrees the בעל קרי only thinks the words. His point is that this silent thinking still counts.

phrases.english: Gemara: Ravina said:
phrases.notes: Start of the גמרא discussing the משנה

phrases.english: This teaches that thinking is like speaking.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ לָאו כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי —
phrases.english: For if it would enter your mind that it is not like speaking —
why does he think the words?
phrases.notes: Why would the משנה have the בעל קרי think שמע at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת הִרְהוּר כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה's rule (Step 24) that a בעל קרי thinks שמע in his heart.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הרהור כדבור דמי: thinking the words counts like saying them.

steps.title: If thinking counts, why not just say it out loud?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבינא: if thinking is the same as speaking, the בעל קרי should simply say the words with his lips.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what are you saying, that thinking is like speaking? Then let him say it with his lips!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבינא's conclusion. If thinking is just like speaking, there seems to be no reason to keep the words silent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If thinking and speaking are equal, holding back speech gains nothing, since the בעל קרי is already 'speaking' in his mind. It makes no sense to allow the thought but forbid the spoken words, so he should simply say them aloud.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him bring it out with his lips (say it aloud)

phrases.english: But what — thinking is like speaking?
Then let him say it with his lips!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's inference in Step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that הרהור כדבור דמי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If thinking equals speaking, there is no point in forbidding speech. The משנה's insistence on silence suggests speech is treated differently.

steps.title: Answer: Like what we found at סיני
steps.stepSummary: Speech out loud is forbidden because of a rabbinic rule modeled on הר סיני, where those who were impure had to purify themselves before the תורה was spoken.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we found at סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבינא. Saying the words aloud is forbidden for a separate reason, based on what happened at הר סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At הר סיני, men who had been with their wives had to immerse before receiving the תורה, which was given through speech. Based on this, the חכמים decreed that a בעל קרי may not say words of תורה out loud until he immerses. Thinking can still count like speaking. Speaking aloud is simply restricted by this decree.

keyTerms.meaning: Mount Sinai, where the תורה was given
Immersion in a מקוה for purity

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not deny that thinking equals speaking. It only explains why the out-loud version is specifically restricted.

phrases.english: As we found at Sinai.
phrases.notes: At Sinai, those impure from relations had to immerse before the תורה was spoken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27 and preserves רבינא's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separate reason: speech aloud is barred by a rabbinic decree modeled on Sinai, not because thinking fails to count.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If thinking equals speaking, there is no reason to forbid saying the words aloud.
steps.terutzMaskana: Saying words of תורה aloud requires purity, as at Sinai. So the בעל קרי thinks silently, and that thinking still counts.

steps.title: רב חסדא: Thinking does not count like speaking
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא learns the opposite from the same משנה: הרהור is not like דיבור. If it were, the בעל קרי would simply say the words.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: Thinking is not like speaking. For if you thought thinking is like speaking, let him say it with his lips!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא disagrees with רבינא. He reads the same משנה and concludes that thinking does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא uses the logic of the challenge in Step 27 as his own position. Since the משנה keeps the בעל קרי silent, thinking must be a lesser thing that does not count as saying the words. On this view, the silent thinking does not fulfill the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who argues with רבינא here

steps.whatToRemember: There are two opposite readings of the same משנה. רבינא says thinking counts like speech, and speech aloud is barred only by the Sinai-based decree. רב חסדא says thinking does not count, or else the בעל קרי would simply speak.
steps.whyThisMatters: The question of whether הרהור כדבור דמי affects whether a person who only thinks שמע or a ברכה has fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
Thinking is not like speaking,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ הִרְהוּר כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי —
phrases.english: for if it would enter your mind that thinking is like speaking —
let him say it with his lips.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר, הִרְהוּר לָאו כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the opposite reading of the משנה from רבינא's in Step 26, using the logic of Step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הרהור לאו כדבור דמי: thinking the words does not count as saying them.

steps.title: If thinking does not count, why think at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא. If הרהור is not like דיבור, the בעל קרי's thinking accomplishes nothing, so why does the משנה tell him to do it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But what are you saying, that thinking is not like speaking? If so, why should he think the words?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב חסדא's reading of the משנה. If thinking does not count as saying שמע, the instruction to think it seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said הרהור is not like דיבור, so the בעל קרי does not fulfill קריאת שמע by thinking it. But the משנה clearly tells him to think it. This step asks what that thinking is for.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But what (are you saying)?' An opening that challenges the position just stated.
He thinks the words in his mind, without saying them.

phrases.english: But what (are you saying)?
that thinking is not considered like speech?
Then why should he think (the words)?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי הִרְהוּר לָאו כְּדִבּוּר דָּמֵי, לָמָּה מְהַרְהֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's view stated in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that הרהור is not like דיבור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If thinking has no legal value, the משנה's instruction to think שמע has no purpose.

steps.title: The thinking keeps him from sitting idle
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that the בעל קרי thinks שמע so that he is not sitting idle while everyone around him is busy reciting it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The point is that everyone else should not be busy with שמע while he sits there doing nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר defends רב חסדא's view. The thinking is not a way of fulfilling the מצוה; it simply keeps the person connected so he is not idle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer changes the purpose of the thinking. It is not a way to fulfill קריאת שמע. It only keeps the person from standing out as idle while the community is involved in שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: So that it should not be (in order to prevent).
Busy with it, involved in it.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר is not saying the בעל קרי fulfills קריאת שמע by thinking. According to this answer, the thinking only prevents idleness, and he has not fulfilled the מצוה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ כׇּל הָעוֹלָם עוֹסְקִין בּוֹ
phrases.english: So that it should not be that everyone is busy with it (שמע)
while he sits idle.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ כׇּל הָעוֹלָם עוֹסְקִין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new purpose for the thinking, separate from fulfilling the מצוה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The thinking must be a way of fulfilling קריאת שמע, so it is pointless if הרהור does not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The thinking only keeps him from being idle while the community recites שמע.

steps.title: Then let him study a different section
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's answer. If the goal is only to avoid idleness, the בעל קרי could just as well study some other section.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him study a different section!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's answer. If the only goal is to keep busy, any learning would do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Avoiding idleness does not explain why it has to be שמע in particular. Any other Torah material would also keep him busy. So the answer seems too general to explain what the משנה requires.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him study or recite (from גרס, to learn).

phrases.english: Then let him study a different section!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's explanation that the thinking is only to avoid idleness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Avoiding idleness can be done with any learning, so it does not explain why he must think שמע specifically.

steps.title: Be involved in what the community is doing
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה answers that a person should be involved in the very thing the community is busy with, so the בעל קרי thinks שמע and not some other section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: He should be busy with the same thing the community is busy with.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה completes the defense. The בעל קרי thinks שמע specifically because that is what everyone around him is doing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal is more than just keeping busy. It is to join in with the community's activity. That is why the instruction is to think שמע and not just any material, and it completes the defense of רב חסדא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: In the matter the community is busy with.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב חסדא, הרהור is not like דיבור. The בעל קרי thinks שמע only so that he will not be idle (רבי אלעזר), and he thinks שמע specifically so that he is joined with what the community is doing (רב אדא בר אהבה).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a practice can exist for the sake of connecting with the community, even when it does not fulfill the מצוה itself.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
(He should be busy) with the matter the community is busy with.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: בְּדָבָר שֶׁהַצִּבּוּר עוֹסְקִין בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Makes the purpose more specific: joining with the community's activity, not just avoiding idleness.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any learning would serve the goal of not being idle.
steps.terutzMaskana: He must be involved in the same matter as the community, which is שמע.
